answer: Random Beacon Admission. Each cycle, a verifiable random function over the prior block hash samples identities into an active cohort, and only sampled agents earn standing; unsampled identities gain nothing that cycle. An attacker must hold many identities across many cycles to gain influence, paying registration and per-cycle upkeep for each without predicting which get selected. The lantern of the beacon shifts each round. A pigment of randomness marks selected agents so colluders cannot precompute a favorable subset. The trellis of eligibility grows only where sampled,
